lesson_scope: Quadrilaterals in coordinate geometry: parallelograms and diagonal bisection, trapezia and parallel gradients, rhombuses and perpendicular diagonal properties, rectangles with perpendicular adjacent sides and areas, kites and diagonal axis of symmetry, and square diagonal perpendicular bisector vertex determination.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding the fourth vertex of a parallelogram using diagonal midpoint bisection.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of determining parallelogram vertex by diagonal bisection.

hints: In a parallelogram, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ bisect each other, so their midpoints are identical.
Set $\dfrac{4 + x_D}{2} = 4 \implies x_D = 4$ and $\dfrac{5 + y_D}{2} = 2.5 \implies y_D = 0$, giving $D(4, 0)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the midpoint $M$ of diagonal $AC$:
$$M = \left(\dfrac{1 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 3}{2}\right) = (4, 2.5)$$

Since the diagonals bisect each other, equate the midpoint of $BD$ to $M(4, 2.5)$:
$$\dfrac{4 + x_D}{2} = 4 \implies 4 + x_D = 8 \implies x_D = 4$$
$$\dfrac{5 + y_D}{2} = 2.5 \implies 5 + y_D = 5 \implies y_D = 0$$
$$D(4, 0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds midpoint of diagonal $AC$ as $M(4, 2.5)$ and sets $\left(\dfrac{4 + x_D}{2}, \dfrac{5 + y_D}{2}\right) = (4, 2.5)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving for an unknown parameter in a trapezium from parallel gradients.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of parallel sides in a trapezium.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the gradient of $AB$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{3 - 1}{5 - 1} = \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$

Equate $m_{CD}$ to $m_{AB}$ and solve for $k$:
$$m_{CD} = \dfrac{k - 8}{2 - 6} = \dfrac{k - 8}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$k - 8 = -2 \implies k = 6$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating rhombus area from diagonal lengths.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of calculating rhombus area from diagonal lengths.

hints: The area of a rhombus is $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times d_1 \times d_2$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the lengths of the two diagonals $PR$ and $QS$:
$$PR = |7 - (-3)| = 10$$
$$QS = |4 - (-4)| = 8$$

Calculate the area of the rhombus:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PR \times QS = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 8 = 40$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: proving a right angle in a rectangle and evaluating its area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of verifying rectangle right angle and area.

walkthrough.text:
Verify the right angle at vertex $B$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{2 - 0}{6 - 0} = \dfrac{1}{3}$$
$$m_{BC} = \dfrac{5 - 2}{5 - 6} = \dfrac{3}{-1} = -3$$
$$m_{AB} \times m_{BC} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times (-3) = -1 \implies \angle ABC = 90^\circ$$

Calculate side lengths and rectangle area:
$$AB = \sqrt{6^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}$$
$$BC = \sqrt{(5 - 6)^2 + (5 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 9} = \sqrt{10}$$
$$\text{Area} = AB \times BC = 2\sqrt{10} \times \sqrt{10} = 20$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of kite symmetry and diagonal midpoint.

hints: The symmetry axis $AC$ bisects diagonal $BD$, so $M(4, 5)$ is the midpoint of $BD$.

walkthrough.text:
Use the midpoint formula for segment $BD$ with midpoint $M(4, 5)$ and endpoint $B(1, 2)$:
$$\dfrac{1 + x_D}{2} = 4$$
$$\dfrac{2 + y_D}{2} = 5$$

Solve each equation for the coordinates of $D$:
$$1 + x_D = 8 \implies x_D = 7$$
$$2 + y_D = 10 \implies y_D = 8$$
$$D(7, 8)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up midpoint equations $\dfrac{1 + x_D}{2} = 4$ and $\dfrac{2 + y_D}{2} = 5$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of square centre and area from diagonal length.

hints: Find the centre $M$ of the square as the midpoint of $AC$: $M = \left(\dfrac{1 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 10}{2}\right) = (4, 6)$.
For a square of diagonal $d$, the area is $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} d^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 = 50$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the centre $M$ as the midpoint of diagonal $AC$:
$$M = \left(\dfrac{1 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 10}{2}\right) = (4, 6)$$

Calculate the squared diagonal length and the area of the square:
$$AC^2 = (7 - 1)^2 + (10 - 2)^2 = 36 + 64 = 100$$
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AC^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 = 50$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: midpoint calculation of diagonal AC and determination of fourth vertex D for a parallelogram.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Midpoint of parallelogram diagonal.

hints: Calculate the midpoint by averaging the coordinates of $A(1, 4)$ and $C(9, 3)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the midpoint of diagonal $AC$:
$$M_{AC} = \left(\dfrac{1 + 9}{2}, \dfrac{4 + 3}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{10}{2}, \dfrac{7}{2}\right) = (5, 3.5)$$

State the coordinates in exact form:
$$M_{AC} = \left(5, \dfrac{7}{2}\right) = (5, 3.5)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding opposite vertex of parallelogram from diagonal midpoint.

hints: Diagonals in a parallelogram bisect each other, so $M_{AC} = M_{BD} = (5, 3.5)$.

walkthrough.text:
Since the diagonals bisect each other, the midpoint of $BD$ is also $M(5, 3.5)$:
$$\dfrac{5 + x_D}{2} = 5$$
$$\dfrac{7 + y_D}{2} = 3.5$$

Solve for the coordinates of $D$:
$$5 + x_D = 10 \implies x_D = 5$$
$$7 + y_D = 7 \implies y_D = 0$$
$$D(5, 0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates midpoint of $BD$ to $M_{AC}$: $\dfrac{5 + x_D}{2} = 5$ and $\dfrac{7 + y_D}{2} = 3.5$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: finding side gradient and equating parallel gradients to solve for unknown parameter in a trapezium.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding gradient of a side.

hints: Use the gradient formula between $A(2, 1)$ and $B(6, 4)$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the gradient of side $AB$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{4 - 1}{6 - 2} = \dfrac{3}{4}$$

State the gradient:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding unknown coordinate from parallel line condition.

hints: Since $CD$ is parallel to $AB$, their gradients are equal: $m_{CD} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the gradient of $CD$ using $C(5, 7)$ and $D(k, 4)$:
$$m_{CD} = \dfrac{4 - 7}{k - 5} = \dfrac{-3}{k - 5}$$

Since $CD$ is parallel to $AB$, equate gradients:
$$\dfrac{-3}{k - 5} = \dfrac{3}{4} \implies 3(k - 5) = -12 \implies k - 5 = -4 \implies k = 1$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: proving a rhombus from four equal side lengths and perpendicular diagonals, then evaluating area using diagonal product.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quadrilateral is a rhombus.

hints: Calculate all four side lengths: $PQ = QR = RS = SP = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5$.
Examine the diagonals: $P(-2, 1)$ to $R(6, 1)$ is horizontal, and $Q(2, 4)$ to $S(2, -2)$ is vertical.
Since all four sides are equal and horizontal/vertical lines are perpendicular, $PQRS$ is a rhombus.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the lengths of all four sides:
$$PQ = \sqrt{(2 - (-2))^2 + (4 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
$$QR = \sqrt{(6 - 2)^2 + (1 - 4)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
$$RS = \sqrt{(2 - 6)^2 + (-2 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
$$SP = \sqrt{(-2 - 2)^2 + (1 - (-2))^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
All four sides are equal in length ($5$ units).

Verify that the diagonals are perpendicular:
$$PR \text{ lies on the horizontal line } y = 1 \implies m_{PR} = 0$$
$$QS \text{ lies on the vertical line } x = 2 \implies m_{QS} \text{ is undefined}$$
Horizontal and vertical lines are perpendicular ($PR \perp QS$). Therefore, $PQRS$ is a rhombus.

ai_rubric.observable: Verifies $PR$ is horizontal (gradient $0$) and $QS$ is vertical, showing diagonals are perpendicular and confirming $PQRS$ is a rhombus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating area of rhombus from diagonal lengths.

hints: Apply the rhombus area formula: $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times d_1 \times d_2$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the lengths of the diagonals $PR$ and $QS$:
$$PR = |6 - (-2)| = 8$$
$$QS = |4 - (-2)| = 6$$

Calculate the area of the rhombus:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PR \times QS = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6 = 24$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: verifying rectangle property via common diagonal midpoints and perpendicular adjacent sides, then computing exact area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quadrilateral is a rectangle.

hints: Show diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ have the same midpoint $M(3.5, 4.5)$, proving $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

walkthrough.text:
Check diagonal midpoints to prove $ABCD$ is a parallelogram:
$$M_{AC} = \left(\dfrac{1 + 6}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 7}{2}\right) = (3.5, 4.5)$$
$$M_{BD} = \left(\dfrac{7 + 0}{2}, \dfrac{4 + 5}{2}\right) = (3.5, 4.5)$$
Since the diagonals bisect each other, $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

Calculate gradients of adjacent sides $AB$ and $BC$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{4 - 2}{7 - 1} = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$$
$$m_{BC} = \dfrac{7 - 4}{6 - 7} = \dfrac{3}{-1} = -3$$
$$m_{AB} \times m_{BC} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times (-3) = -1 \implies \angle ABC = 90^\circ$$
Since $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with a right angle, it is a rectangle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating area of rectangle from side lengths.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the lengths of the adjacent sides $AB$ and $BC$:
$$AB = \sqrt{(7 - 1)^2 + (4 - 2)^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}$$
$$BC = \sqrt{(6 - 7)^2 + (7 - 4)^2} = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{10}$$

Calculate the area of the rectangle:
$$\text{Area} = AB \times BC = 2\sqrt{10} \times \sqrt{10} = 2 \times 10 = 20$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: finding trapezium vertex parameter from perpendicular corner condition and determining 4th vertex from parallel side constraints.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding parameter from perpendicularity condition.

hints: Since $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$, the perpendicular gradient of $BC$ is $m_{BC} = -\dfrac{1}{-1/2} = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate gradient of side $AB$ and determine the perpendicular gradient of $BC$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{3 - 0}{0 - 6} = -\dfrac{3}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$m_{BC} = -\dfrac{1}{-1/2} = 2$$

Set up the gradient formula for $BC$ using $B(0, 3)$ and $C(h, 3h)$:
$$m_{BC} = \dfrac{3h - 3}{h - 0} = 2$$
$$3h - 3 = 2h \implies h = 3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds gradient $m_{AB} = \dfrac{3 - 0}{0 - 6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ and sets perpendicular gradient $m_{BC} = 2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding coordinates of 4th vertex from parallel line constraints.

hints: With $h = 3$, vertex $C$ is $(3, 9)$. Side $CD$ is horizontal, so $y_D = 9$.
Side $AD$ is parallel to $BC$, so $m_{AD} = m_{BC} = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
With $h = 3$, $C(h, 3h) = (3, 9)$. Since side $CD$ is parallel to the $x$-axis, the $y$-coordinate of $D$ is constant:
$$y_D = y_C = 9$$

Since $AD$ is parallel to $BC$, $m_{AD} = 2$:
$$\dfrac{9 - 0}{x_D - 6} = 2 \implies 9 = 2(x_D - 6) = 2x_D - 12$$
$$2x_D = 21 \implies x_D = \dfrac{21}{2} = 10.5$$
$$D\left(\dfrac{21}{2}, 9\right)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies $y_D = y_C = 9$ from $CD$ parallel to $x$-axis and sets $m_{AD} = \dfrac{9 - 0}{x_D - 6} = 2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: kite coordinate problem finding equations of perpendicular diagonals, calculating their intersection, and doubling from origin to find vertex B.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding equations of perpendicular diagonals in a kite.

hints: The diagonal $OB$ is perpendicular to $AC$, so $m_{OB} = -\dfrac{1}{-3/4} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.
Since $OB$ passes through the origin $(0, 0)$, its equation is $y = \dfrac{4}{3}x$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate gradient and equation of diagonal $AC$:
$$m_{AC} = \dfrac{0 - 6}{8 - 0} = -\dfrac{6}{8} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$
$$y - 6 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 0) \implies y = -\dfrac{3}{4}x + 6$$

Calculate gradient and equation of diagonal $OB$:
$$m_{OB} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{AC}} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$
Since $OB$ passes through $(0, 0)$:
$$y = \dfrac{4}{3}x$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses perpendicular gradient $m_{OB} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ through origin to obtain $y = \dfrac{4}{3}x$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding intersection of perpendicular diagonals in a kite.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the two line equations to find the intersection point $M$:
$$\dfrac{4}{3}x = -\dfrac{3}{4}x + 6$$
$$\left(\dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{3}{4}\right)x = 6 \implies \dfrac{25}{12}x = 6 \implies x = \dfrac{72}{25} = 2.88$$

Calculate the corresponding $y$-coordinate:
$$y = \dfrac{4}{3}\left(\dfrac{72}{25}\right) = \dfrac{96}{25} = 3.84$$
$$M(2.88, 3.84)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding kite vertex from diagonal bisection property.

hints: The symmetry axis $AC$ bisects the diagonal $OB$, so $M(2.88, 3.84)$ is the midpoint of $OB$.

walkthrough.text:
Since $AC$ is the axis of symmetry, it bisects diagonal $OB$, making $M(2.88, 3.84)$ the midpoint of $OB$:
$$\dfrac{0 + x_B}{2} = 2.88 \implies x_B = 5.76$$
$$\dfrac{0 + y_B}{2} = 3.84 \implies y_B = 7.68$$
$$B(5.76, 7.68)$$

Express in exact fractional form:
$$B\left(\dfrac{144}{25}, \dfrac{192}{25}\right) = (5.76, 7.68)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Doubles midpoint coordinates from origin to obtain $B(5.76, 7.68)$ (or $B\left(\dfrac{144}{25}, \dfrac{192}{25}\right)$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: square diagonal perpendicular bisector derivation, finding the remaining two vertices via distance constraints from centre, and calculating area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding square centre and equation of perpendicular diagonal.

hints: Find the centre $M$ of the square as the midpoint of $AC$: $M = \left(\dfrac{2 + 8}{2}, \dfrac{1 + 5}{2}\right) = (5, 3)$.
Form the line equation through $M(5, 3)$ with gradient $-\dfrac{3}{2}$: $y - 3 = -\dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5) \implies 3x + 2y = 21$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the centre $M$ of the square (midpoint of diagonal $AC$):
$$M = \left(\dfrac{2 + 8}{2}, \dfrac{1 + 5}{2}\right) = (5, 3)$$

Find the gradient of $AC$ and the perpendicular gradient of diagonal $BD$:
$$m_{AC} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{8 - 2} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$$
$$m_{BD} = -\dfrac{1}{2/3} = -\dfrac{3}{2}$$

Form the equation of the diagonal line $BD$ passing through $M(5, 3)$:
$$y - 3 = -\dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5)$$
$$2(y - 3) = -3(x - 5) \implies 2y - 6 = -3x + 15$$
$$3x + 2y = 21$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds gradient $m_{AC} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{8 - 2} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ and uses perpendicular gradient $m_{BD} = -\dfrac{3}{2}$.
Forms line equation through $M(5, 3)$ to obtain $3x + 2y = 21$ (or $y = -\dfrac{3}{2}x + \dfrac{21}{2}$).

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding remaining vertices of square from centre and calculating area.

hints: The distance from centre $M(5, 3)$ to any vertex is $r = \dfrac{AC}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6^2 + 4^2}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{52}}{2} = \sqrt{13}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the squared half-diagonal length from centre $M(5, 3)$ to vertices:
$$AC^2 = (8 - 2)^2 + (5 - 1)^2 = 36 + 16 = 52$$
$$r^2 = \left(\dfrac{AC}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{52}{4} = 13$$

Substitute $y - 3 = -\dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5)$ into the distance relation $(x - 5)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 13$:
$$(x - 5)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}(x - 5)\right)^2 = 13$$
$$(x - 5)^2 + \dfrac{9}{4}(x - 5)^2 = 13$$
$$\dfrac{13}{4}(x - 5)^2 = 13 \implies (x - 5)^2 = 4$$
$$x - 5 = \pm 2 \implies x = 7 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 3$$

Find corresponding $y$-values and state vertices $B$ and $D$:
$$\text{When } x = 7: y = 3 - \dfrac{3}{2}(2) = 0 \implies B(7, 0)$$
$$\text{When } x = 3: y = 3 - \dfrac{3}{2}(-2) = 6 \implies D(3, 6)$$

Calculate the area of the square:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AC^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 52 = 26$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets distance from $M(5, 3)$ equal to $\sqrt{13}$ on $3x + 2y = 21$: $(x - 5)^2 + \dfrac{9}{4}(x - 5)^2 = 13$.
